What Credit Score Do You Actually Need to Buy a Home in Southern California?

The Real Minimums, What Each Score Gets You, and How to Improve Faster Than You Think

By Rudy Corona · February 7, 2026

Credit Score Anxiety Is Real. Let's Cut Through It.

Most people who think their credit is a problem are closer to buying than they believe. The ones who do have work to do can usually get there faster than they expect. Here is the real picture on credit scores and home buying.

The Minimum Credit Score for Each Loan Program

Loan ProgramMinimum ScoreNotes
FHA Loan580 for 3.5% down; 500–579 for 10% downMost flexible
Conventional Loan620 minimum; 680+ for best ratesBest terms at 720+
VA LoanNo official minimum; lenders typically 580–620Eligible veterans
USDA Loan640 typicalRural and qualifying suburban
CalHFA Programs640 to 660 depending on programCalifornia DPA

What Your Credit Score Actually Costs You

The minimum gets you in the door. But your score also determines your interest rate and thus your monthly payment. The difference between a 640 and a 760 credit score can be roughly $568 per month on a $500,000 loan — over 30 years, more than $200,000 in extra interest. Your credit score is worth investing in before you buy.

How to Improve Your Score Before You Buy

  • Pay down credit card balances (utilization is 30% of your score).
  • Do not miss a payment; set up autopay for minimums.
  • Do not close old accounts; length of history matters.
  • Avoid new credit applications in the 6–12 months before you apply.
  • Check your report at AnnualCreditReport.com and dispute errors.

Meaningful improvement often takes 3–6 months. I do credit reviews for every client. Get a free credit review with Rudy Corona — find out where you stand and what it takes to reach your goal.
